Part 1: Synthesis of Forward Primer (AGTTGGAGCTGGTGA)

    Step 1.1: Initial Bead Preparation
        Option 1.1.1: Wash immobilized initiator oligonucleotide beads with 1X B&W Buffer.
            - Component A: Immobilized initiator oligonucleotide on beads
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            (operational details: Use a magnetic stand to separate the beads for 1 minute. Remove the supernatant. Add 1X B&W Buffer, resuspend the beads, separate, and discard the supernatant. Repeat wash cycles 2-3 times prior to initiating synthesis.)

    Step 1.2: Coupling Reaction
        Option 1.2.1: TdT-mediated incorporation of a 3'-ONH2-dNTP.
            - Component A: Immobilized oligonucleotide on beads (from previous step)
            - Component B: ZaTdT-R335L-K337G (at 2 mg/mL final concentration)
            - Component C: 3'-ONH2-dNTP (specific to the cycle, at 0.50 mM final concentration)
            - Component D: CoCl2 (at 0.50 mM final concentration)
            - Component E: phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) (at 50 mM final concentration)
            - Component F: NaCl (at 100 mM final concentration)
            (operational details: Combine all components using HPLC-grade water. Ensure reagents are free from aldehyde/ketone contamination. Incubate the reaction mixture at 30 °C for 5 min with gentle tilting and rotation to keep beads suspended. The specific 3'-ONH2-dNTP used is determined by the synthesis cycle.)

    Step 1.3: Post-Coupling Wash
        Option 1.3.1: Wash beads to remove coupling reaction components.
            - Component A: Beads from Step 1.2
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            (operational details: Use a magnetic stand to separate the beads for 1 minute. Remove the supernatant. Add 1X B&W Buffer, resuspend the beads, separate, and discard the supernatant. Repeat wash cycles 2-3 times.)

    Step 1.4: Deblocking Reaction
        Option 1.4.1: Cleavage of the 3'-ONH2 protecting group.
            - Component A: Washed beads from Step 1.3
            - Component B: Cleavage Reagent
                - Recipe: 700 mM NaNO2 in 1 M aqueous sodium acetate buffer, pH 5.5
            (operational details: Resuspend the beads in the Cleavage Reagent and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes with gentle rotation. This step may be repeated to ensure complete cleavage.)

    Step 1.5: Post-Deblocking Wash
        Option 1.5.1: Wash beads to remove deblocking agent.
            - Component A: Beads from Step 1.4
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            (operational details: Use a magnetic stand to separate the beads for 1 minute. Remove the deblocking buffer. Add 1X B&W Buffer, resuspend the beads, separate, and discard the supernatant. Repeat wash cycles 2-3 times.)

    Step 1.6: Iterative Synthesis Execution for Forward Primer (AGTTGGAGCTGGTGA)
        Option 1.6.1: Repeat synthesis cycles for each nucleotide in the target sequence.
            (operational details: Repeat Steps 1.2 through 1.5 for the 15 nucleotides of the forward primer sequence. The specific 3'-ONH2-dNTP used in Step 1.2 (Component C) is changed for each cycle according to the target sequence AGTTGGAGCTGGTGA. The number of parallel syntheses should be adjusted as needed for downstream applications, e.g., 20 parallel reactions.)
            - Cycle 1: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A
            - Cycle 2: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 3: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 4: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 5: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 6: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 7: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A
            - Cycle 8: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 9: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C
            - Cycle 10: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 11: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 12: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 13: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 14: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 15: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A

Incubate the reaction mixture at 30 °C for 5 min with gentle tilting and rotation to keep beads suspended. The specific 3'-ONH2-dNTP used is determined by the synthesis cycle.)

    Step 2.3: Post-Coupling Wash
        Option 2.3.1: Wash beads to remove coupling reaction components.
            - Component A: Beads from Step 2.2
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            (operational details: Use a magnetic stand to separate the beads for 1 minute. Remove the supernatant. Add 1X B&W Buffer, resuspend the beads, separate, and discard the supernatant. Repeat wash cycles 2-3 times.)

            - Component A: Washed beads from Step 2.3
            - Component B: Cleavage Reagent
                - Recipe: 700 mM NaNO2 in 1 M aqueous sodium acetate buffer, pH 5.5
            (operational details: Resuspend the beads in the Cleavage Reagent and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes with gentle rotation. This step may be repeated to ensure complete cleavage.)

    Step 2.5: Post-Deblocking Wash
        Option 2.5.1: Wash beads to remove deblocking agent.
            - Component A: Beads from Step 2.4
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            (operational details: Use a magnetic stand to separate the beads for 1 minute. Remove the deblocking buffer. Add 1X B&W Buffer, resuspend the beads, separate, and discard the supernatant. Repeat wash cycles 2-3 times.)

    Step 2.6: Iterative Synthesis Execution for Reverse Primer (GAATGGTCCTGCACC)
        Option 2.6.1: Repeat synthesis cycles for each nucleotide in the target sequence.
            (operational details: Repeat Steps 2.2 through 2.5 for the 15 nucleotides of the reverse primer sequence. The specific 3'-ONH2-dNTP used in Step 2.2 (Component C) is changed for each cycle according to the target sequence GAATGGTCCTGCACC. The number of parallel syntheses should be adjusted as needed for downstream applications, e.g., 20 parallel reactions.)
            - Cycle 1: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 2: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A
            - Cycle 3: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A
            - Cycle 4: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 5: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 6: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 7: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 8: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C
            - Cycle 9: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C
            - Cycle 10: Use 3'-ONH2-dTTP for T
            - Cycle 11: Use 3'-ONH2-dGTP for G
            - Cycle 12: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C
            - Cycle 13: Use 3'-ONH2-dATP for A
            - Cycle 14: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C
            - Cycle 15: Use 3'-ONH2-dCTP for C

Part 3: Post-Synthesis Primer Cleavage and Quantification

    Step 3.1: Preparation of Digestion Mix
        Option 3.1.1: Prepare USER enzyme digestion mix.
            - Component A: USER enzyme
            - Component B: TE buffer
            (operational details: Add 1 uL of USER enzyme to 49 uL of TE buffer to prepare the Digestion Mix.)

    Step 3.2: Bead Pooling and Washing
        Option 3.2.1: Pool and wash beads post-synthesis.
            - Component A: Magnetic beads with synthesized primers (from Part 1 or Part 2)
            - Component B: 1X B&W Buffer
                - Recipe: 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 M NaCl, 0.1% Tween-20
            - Component C: TE buffer
            (operational details: Combine the magnetic beads from exactly 20 synthesis tubes into a single collection tube. Add 5uL of 1X B&W buffer from each tube before pooling. Place the collection tube on a magnetic rack, remove the supernatant, and rinse the beads once with TE Buffer. Remove the supernatant before proceeding.)

    Step 3.3: Enzymatic Digestion and Primer Collection
        Option 3.3.1: Digest DNA from beads using USER enzyme in two rounds.
            - Component A: Washed beads from Step 3.2
            - Component B: Digestion Mix (from Step 3.1)
            - Component C: USER enzyme
            (operational details: The digestion and collection process is performed in two sequential rounds to maximize product yield.)
            - Round 1: Take the tube containing beads off the magnetic rack. Add 30 uL of the Digestion Mix. Mix well and place on a heatershaker at 37°C and 1000 rpm for 30 minutes. Add 0.4 uL of USER enzyme, mix, and incubate for another 30 minutes. Mix again, then incubate for a final 30 minutes. Place the tube on the magnetic rack and transfer the supernatant to a new collection tube.
            - Round 2: Remove the tube containing the beads from the magnet. Add 15 uL of the Digestion Mix to the beads. Repeat the incubation process from Round 1 (30 min incubation, add 0.4 uL USER enzyme, 30 min incubation, mix, 30 min incubation). Place the tube on the magnetic rack, collect the supernatant, and combine it with the supernatant from Round 1 to obtain the final product solution.

    Step 3.4: Preparation of Qubit Working Solution
        Option 3.4.1: Prepare Qubit working solution for fluorometric quantification.
            - Component A: Qubit Reagent
            - Component B: Qubit Buffer
            (operational details: Add 1 uL of Qubit Reagent to 199 uL of Qubit Buffer. Mix well by pipetting to prepare the working solution.)

    Step 3.5: Sample Preparation for Quantification
        Option 3.5.1: Dilute the final product solution for measurement.
            - Component A: final product solution (from Step 3.3)
            - Component B: Qubit Working Solution (from Step 3.4)
            (operational details: Add 1 uL of the final product solution to 199 uL of the Qubit Working Solution. Mix well by pipetting.)

    Step 3.6: Quantification Measurement
        Option 3.6.1: Measure DNA concentration using a fluorometer.
            - Component A: Diluted sample from Step 3.5
            (operational details: Seal the tube tightly and centrifuge briefly to ensure the liquid is at the bottom and bubbles are removed. Incubate the mixture in the dark at room temperature for 2 minutes. Place the tube in the fluorometer and measure the concentration.)
